Title: Tickle to Talk with Moji Mi | The Toy Insider
# Tickle to Talk with Moji Mi. 685_1_2Aside from adding some playful zest to an otherwise dry text message, emojis give true value to cyber communication by adding personality to blasé texts and minimizing the risk of misinterpretation. In layman’s terms, emojis are ridiculous fun! Now, with Moji Mi, kids can now enjoy emoticons and emojis in a tangible form. Designed for kids ages 6 and up, Moji Mi from Little Kids are cute plastic characters with a lot to say. They’re basically living emoticons, and unless your kid is friendly with Sheldon James Plankton, they’ll quickly become their most mini friend. Moji Mi are adorable little creatures, each with their own splash of color and dose of personality. And since no two Mojis are the same, collecting them all is as important as ever. Little Kids pretty much covered all the bases, making sure there’s a Moji Mi fit for every kid. Each Moji Mi sports four tiny strands of hair that act as a communication channel. When kids tickle their hair, they’ll make fun sounds that express how they’re feeling, and when they cross the hairs of two Mojis, they’ll communicate with each other. If kids leave their Moji Mi idle for too long, they’ll even start to snore. I can compare it to the kind of sounds Minions make, or how I would imagine Mike Tyson would speak after a shot of Novocain. Either way, the gibberish is comical and adds to the fun. I played around with two different Moji personalities: Abuzz with Excitement and Rock and Roll. With parents’ permission, kids can head online to explore fun Moji Mi games and other activities. Amanda Toy Headshot Nov 2024 Scaled. Amanda Toy Headshot Nov 2024 Scaled #### Vice President of Membership and Partnerships. ###### atoy@michamber.com. As VP of membership and partnerships at the MI Chamber, Amanda leads the team responsible for membership and business solutions offered to MI Chamber members. Because she communicates with members daily, Amanda has the opportunity to understand their business needs and find partners that can offer relevant solutions. If you ask her colleagues, they may describe her as the team’s head cheerleader, often encouraging individuals to use their unique gifts to be growth-minded. Prior to joining the MI Chamber, Amanda spent a decade in nonprofit management optimizing her servant leadership style, and 15 years in the for-profit hospitality industry in operations and business development. Amanda holds a B.A. from *The* School of Hospitality Business at Michigan State University. She is a winner of the Emerging Profssional of the Year award from the Michigan Society Association Executives (MSAE). She is also a Board member of the Association of State Chamber Professionals (ASCP) and is active in her church community. Her favorite part about working at the MI Chamber, other than knowing the team works each day to advance the MI Chamber mission, is meeting Michigan business leaders from all over our state — each has a passion, a leadership strategy and a story to tell. She loves connecting leaders where their passions intersect; from the U.P. to the west coast to SE Michigan and everywhere between.
